findings.description: The hook now honours LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 from its own environment and tags the audit row with replay:true (also at the FR-MERGE-2, FR-SZ and FR-SZ2 allow rows). Nothing checks that the caller is the corpus runner. Model-side exposure is limited because a `LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 cmd` prefix inside the Bash tool string does not reach the hook's environment, but any process that controls the hook environment (an operator shell that exported it once for a corpus run and then launched Claude Code, an `env` block in a settings file, a wrapper in settings.local.json) tags every real block as replay for the whole session.
findings.failure_mode: If guard-yield.sh drops replay rows from real_blocks_30d, a session launched with the variable still set reports zero real blocks for guards that did fire, and the 30-day yield that loa-status.sh displays understates floor guards silently.
findings.suggested_fix: Have run-corpus.sh pass an explicit marker the hook can verify (for example a per-run token written to .run/ and compared, or invoke the hook with a `--replay` argument), and have guard-yield.sh count replay rows in a separate column rather than discarding them so a mis-set variable is visible.

findings.description: Adding a `paths:` frontmatter block turns an always-loaded rule into a path-scoped one. Claude Code loads path-scoped rules only when a matching file is read or edited. The stash rule is about `git stash` invocations typed into the Bash tool, which touch no *.sh or *.bats file, so in the common case (a model stashing during a sprint without editing shell scripts) the prose guard is no longer in context. The fence FR-1.2b still blocks the swallowed-output forms, but plain `git stash push`/`pop` around pre-commit hooks, which the rule warns about, is prose-only.
findings.failure_mode: Stash wraps in Bash-only sessions proceed without the rule's guidance; the index-shift data-loss pattern the rule exists for (recurred cycle-122) can recur unobserved.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep stash-safety.md unscoped (drop `paths:`), or scope it to a glob that also matches the planning and implementing skill files that are read in every sprint, and add a rule-paths.bats case asserting the stash rule has no narrow path scope.

findings.description: The app-zone permission for /implement changes from read to read-write with no mention in the PR, the sprint plan, or a DEC row. The change is probably correct in substance (the implement skill is where app writes are sanctioned, and the implement gate asks outside a run), but the skill-invariants rule in this same diff states that zone frontmatter is the path-level control for app writes, and floor.yaml protects `implement_gate.*` as a floor key, so a silent widening of the zone declaration in a guard-register PR is the kind of change the register is meant to surface.
findings.failure_mode: Reviewers and the guard register cannot tell whether the widening was intended; if any validator or future profile check reads `zones.app.permission`, the behaviour change lands untracked.
findings.suggested_fix: Either revert the line out of this PR or add a one-line note in the PR description and a DEC row citing why /implement declares read-write for the app zone.

findings.cross_file_justification: The template comment immediately above these lines says the `⇐` annotation becomes the `--deps` flag when the task is created as a bead. The `· kind:` token is appended after the blockers on the same line, so any consumer that takes the remainder of the line after `⇐` as the deps value now receives `none · kind: mechanical`.
findings.description: The kind token is placed after the blockers annotation on the task line. The validator in this PR parses the kind token (tests pass), but the bead-creation path that reads `⇐ {Task 1.1} | none` into `--deps` is not in the diff and was not shown to tolerate trailing text. The third placeholder line also carries a literal `kind: {mechanical|judgment|operator}` which does not match the one-token rule if copied verbatim.
findings.failure_mode: Bead creation from a plan written against the new template either fails the edge-or-none rule or creates a dependency on a non-existent task named `none · kind: mechanical`.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify the deps extractor stops at ` · ` (or move `kind:` before `⇐`), add a sprint-kinds.bats case with both annotations on one line, and make the placeholder line use a concrete token.

findings.description: Confirming the primary reviewer's concern 2 from jq semantics (file truncated in my view, line not visible). `(.constraints // []) |= map(...)` is not a valid update path when `.constraints` is null or absent: jq evaluates the alternative `[]`, which is a value, not a path, and errors with 'Invalid path expression with result []'. With the error swallowed inside `apply_toggles || exit 2`, the arm run exits 2 and leaves `constraints.json.tmp` behind.
findings.failure_mode: Any task fixture without a `constraints` key makes the karpathy toggle arm fail with exit 2 and no diagnostic, and the comparison for that arm is reported as invalid rather than as a result.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `.constraints |= ((. // []) | map(...))`, write the tmp file via a trap-cleaned path, and add an execute-agent.bats case with a fixture lacking `constraints`.

findings.description: Confirming the primary reviewer's concern 1 (file truncated in my view). Sourcing `heredoc-classifier.sh` inline means any `exit` in it or in what it sources ends guard-yield.sh with that status. If the status is 0, `--check` mode (gate:guard-origins, registered as a CI gate in guard-origins.yaml) returns success having checked nothing, and the register is neither verified nor regenerated.
findings.failure_mode: A later edit to the classifier or the fence's lib-only entry path turns the guard-origins CI gate into a no-op without a failing test.
findings.suggested_fix: Probe the library in a subshell first (`( source "$HEREDOC_LIB" ) || die 5`), or source it with `BDB_LIB_ONLY=1` set and assert a known function is defined afterwards, exiting 5 if not; add a guard-yield.bats case with a stub classifier that calls `exit 0`.
